nodes.title: Browser process aborts (NOTREACHED "Unsuitable process reused for site") when an MV3 extension service worker is re-woken via startWorkerForScope
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the Contributing Guidelines for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the Code of Conduct that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.0.0 (Chromium 150.0.7871.46)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26.6 (25G72), arm64 (M3 Pro)

### What arch are you using?

arm64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown — first observed on 43.0.0. I have not bisected.

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No. Chrome loads the same extension without incident. Note that Electron runs with
`--disable-features=SpareRendererForSitePerProcess`, which Chrome does not, and this
plausibly makes process reuse more aggressive here (see Additional Information).

### Expected Behavior

Waking a stopped MV3 extension background service worker — which
`session.serviceWorkers.startWorkerForScope()` does, and which
`electron-chrome-extensions` does on every `chrome.*` event delivery — should either
start the worker or fail gracefully.

### Actual Behavior

The **browser process** aborts with `EXC_BREAKPOINT (SIGTRAP)` on `CrBrowserMain`.
The whole app disappears; this is not a renderer crash and it is not catchable from
JavaScript.

The abort is a Chromium `NOTREACHED` in
`content/browser/renderer_host/render_process_host_impl.cc:5423`:

```cpp
if (render_process_host && !RenderProcessHostImpl::MayReuseAndIsSuitable(
                               render_process_host, site_instance)) {
  …
  NOTREACHED() << "Unsuitable process reused for site " << site_info;
}
```

Symbolicated stack (Breakpad symbols from the 43.0.0 release, framework UUID
`4C4C443A55553144A1ACB7F47BA94945`):

```
base::MessagePumpCFRunLoopBase::RunWorkSource
  mojo::internal::MultiplexRouter::Accept
    storage::mojom::ServiceWorkerStorageControl_FindRegistrationForScope_ForwardToCallback::Accept
      content::ServiceWorkerRegistry::DidFindRegistrationForScope
        content::ServiceWorkerContextWrapper::DidFindRegistrationForFindImpl
          content::(anonymous namespace)::FoundRegistrationForStartWorker
            content::ServiceWorkerVersion::StartWorker
              content::ServiceWorkerVersion::StartWorkerInternal
                content::EmbeddedWorkerInstance::Start                    (embedded_worker_instance.cc:289)
                  content::ServiceWorkerProcessManager::AllocateWorkerProcess (service_worker_process_manager.cc:145)
                    content::SiteInstanceImpl::GetOrCreateProcess            (site_instance_impl.cc:482)
                      content::RenderProcessHostImpl::GetProcessHostForSiteInstance
                        NOTREACHED()                                        (render_process_host_impl.cc:5423)
```

`FoundRegistrationForStartWorker` is referenced from exactly one function in
Chromium — `ServiceWorkerContextWrapper::StartWorkerForScope` — which is the backing
of `session.serviceWorkers.startWorkerForScope()`. So the crash is specific to that
API, not to service workers in general: a website's service worker starting through
navigation/fetch/push does not take this path.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

**Reproduction shape.** Load an MV3 extension with a background service worker into a
`persist:` session, then browse normally. The MV3 worker idles out after ~30s and is
re-woken on the next `chrome.*` event via `startWorkerForScope`. The crash happens on
one of those wakes. It is not deterministic per wake — many wakes succeed — but it
recurs reliably over a session. I have five crash reports with **byte-identical**
stacks (same image offsets in every frame), with uptimes from 2m22s to 2h14m.

I instrumented `session.serviceWorkers.on('running-status-changed')` to log the worker
lifecycle. The last events before one crash:

```
18:38:30.818Z stopping v0 chrome-extension://<id>/
18:38:30.820Z stopped  v0 chrome-extension://<id>/
   …crash 27 seconds later, mid-browsing, with no extension install/enable in between
```

No `starting` line is logged for the fatal wake, because the running-status observer
fires after process allocation — the abort happens first. A benign cycle earlier in
the same session shows `stopped` → `starting` 138 ms later, i.e. the same wake path
succeeding.

**Where I think it goes wrong.** `shell/browser/electron_browser_client.cc`
special-cases extensions in three process-model hooks:

- `ShouldUseProcessPerSite` returns true only for extensions, so the extension's
  service worker `SiteInstance` resolves through the process-per-site map.
- `DoesSiteRequireDedicatedProcess` returns true for extensions.
- `IsSuitableHost` compares a process "privilege" derived from
  `extensions::ProcessMap`.

My hypothesis is that after an MV3 worker stops, the process-per-site map still points
at the process that hosted the extension, while `extensions::ProcessMap` no longer
records that process as the extension's. The privilege comparison then fails,
`MayReuseAndIsSuitable` returns false, and the `NOTREACHED` fires. That would explain
the one distinguishing feature of this bug: it never fails on the worker's *first*
start, only on a later wake.

I have not verified that mechanism directly — the offending `site_info` is stored via
`SetCrashKeyString` and, in a release build, the streamed `NOTREACHED` message is
compiled out, so it does not reach stderr and macOS `.ips` files do not carry crash
keys. If a maintainer can point me at the right instrumentation I am happy to gather
more.

**Impact.** Any Electron app loading an MV3 extension is exposed, since
`electron-chrome-extensions` calls `startWorkerForScope` on every event delivery to a
stopped worker. The failure kills the browser process, so an app cannot defend against
it — there is no JS-observable error, and no argument to `loadExtension` or
`startWorkerForScope` changes the outcome.

Unfortunately, without a way to reproduce this issue, we're unable to continue investigation. This issue has been closed and will not be monitored further. If you're able to provide a minimal test case that reproduces this issue on a [supported version of Electron](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/electron-timelines#timeline) please open a new issue and include instructions for reproducing the issue.

nodes.title: Potential DLL Side-Loading Vulnerability in Electron 35 on Windows
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

35.0.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

win 11

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

Electron applications should not allow Windows system DLLs or optional DLLs to be loaded from the application installation directory unless explicitly intended. DLL loading should use secure Windows DLL loading mechanisms and trusted system locations to prevent DLL side-loading.

### Actual Behavior

The custom DLL is executed during application startup, resulting in arbitrary code execution (for example, Calculator launching from the DLL payload).

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

**Summary:**
- We observed behavior that may indicate a DLL side-loading vulnerability in Electron 30 on Windows.

**Environment**
- Electron: 35.0.0
- Platform: Windows 11 (64-bit)
- Packaging: Electron Forge (MSI)

**Steps to Reproduce**
- Build and install an Electron application.
- Monitor the application startup using Process Monitor.
- Observe that Windows probes the application installation directory for optional system DLLs, including:
   - CRYPTSP.dll
   - dbghelp.dll
   - version.dll
   - winhttp.dll
   - userenv.dll
   - dbgcore.dll

- Create a custom DLL (proof of concept) with a payload  (for example, launching Calculator).
- Rename the DLL to match one of the DLL names observed during startup (for example, CRYPTSP.dll).
- Copy the DLL into the application's installation directory.
- Launch the application.

**Observed Behavior**
- The custom DLL is executed during application startup, resulting in arbitrary code execution (for example, Calculator launching from the DLL payload).

<!-- end-of-life -->

The version of Electron reported in this issue has reached end-of-life and is [no longer supported](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/electron-timelines#timeline). If you're still experiencing this issue on a [supported version](https://www.electronjs.org/releases/stable) of Electron, please update this issue to reflect that version of Electron.

Now adding the https://github.com/electron/electron/labels/blocked%2Fneed-info%20%E2%9D%8C label for this reason. This issue will be closed in 10 days if the above is not addressed.

Hi! Thanks for the update.

I can confirm that this issue is still present on Electron 35.x as well. I've verified that the behavior persists after upgrading to a supported version of Electron.

I've updated the issue accordingly. Please let me know if you need any additional information, logs, or a minimal reproduction to help investigate further.

These DLL loads come from Chromium and they do not change them per their threat model:

https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src.git/+/master/docs/security/faq.md#why-arent-physically_local-attacks-in-chromes-threat-model

nodes.title: OSR useSharedTexture: details.texture is always null on Linux with the NVIDIA proprietary driver
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 43.2.0 ### What operating system(s) are you using? Ubuntu ### Operating System Version Ubuntu 22.04.5 and Ubuntu 24.04.4, X11 (kernel 6.8.0-136) ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version _No response_ ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? I don't know how to test ### Expected Behavior With `webPreferences.offscreen.useSharedTexture: true`, the `paint` event should provide `details.texture` as an `OffscreenSharedTexture`, with `textureInfo.handle.nativePixmap.planes[].fd` on Linux. ### Actual Behavior `details.texture` is always `null` on Linux with the NVIDIA proprietary driver. The `paint` event fires normally, but every frame silently falls back to the CPU bitmap path, so the GPU-accelerated capture mode is unusable. There is no error thrown and no warning — the only way to notice is checking `details.texture` yourself. The same code returns a shared texture on Windows and macOS. ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/sdkv2/94dec53fa8397ef82cd2e218dfdf9a36 ### Additional Information Reproduced on **Electron 43.2.0 and 40.10.6**, on four separate machines (RTX 3060), across both Ubuntu versions, three NVIDIA driver versions (575.51.03, 575.57.08, 580.95.05), two libgbm versions (23.2.1 and 25.2.8), and three X server setups (Xvfb, hand-configured Xorg with `nvidia_drv.so`, and a full SDDM/KDE session). Result was identical in every combination. `--enable-features=Vulkan` is often suggested as the NVIDIA workaround. It did not produce a shared texture in any configuration I tried, and it additionally disabled WebGL2 entirely — for an app using OSR to capture WebGL content, that trade is not usable. Note for anyone else testing this: Xvfb provides no DRI3, so it can never work — but hardware GL still reports a real GPU renderer string under it, which makes it look like a working setup.
In-depth investigation

`details.texture` is explicitly `null` rather than `undefined` (verified by dumping the whole paint callback: `arg[0] = { texture: null, preventDefault: …, defaultPrevented: false }`), so `offscreen_use_shared_texture_` is being set correctly in C++ — viz simply never delivers a usable frame to `OnFrameCaptured`. With `--enable-logging=stderr --v=1`, ANGLE reports: ``` ERROR:ui/gl/egl_util.cc:92] EGL Driver message (Error) : Internal Vulkan error (-8): A requested feature is not supported, in third_party/angle/src/libANGLE/renderer/vulkan/linux/DmaBufImageSiblingVkLinux.cpp, initImpl:616. ``` `-8` is `VK_ERROR_FEATURE_NOT_PRESENT`. (Line is `initImpl:616` on Electron 43.2.0 and `initImpl:614` on 40.10.6 — same function.) The likely cause is what the capture pool asks GBM for. `RenderableGpuMemoryBufferVideoFramePool` allocates with `requires_cpu_access = true` → `SCANOUT_CPU_READ_WRITE` → `GBM_BO_USE_LINEAR | GBM_BO_USE_SCANOUT | GBM_BO_USE_TEXTURING`, notably *without* `GBM_BO_USE_RENDERING` (`ui/gfx/linux/gbm_util.cc`). Chromium's own comment in `media/video/renderable_gpu_memory_buffer_video_frame_pool.cc` predicts this failure and names the vendor: > "On Linux, `GBM_BO_USE_LINEAR` (implied by `SCANOUT_CPU_READ_WRITE`) can prevent GPU rendering on some drivers, notably NVIDIA's GBM driver, because it disables `GBM_BO_USE_RENDERING`." So the buffer is allocated, but NVIDIA's Vulkan will not import a LINEAR/SCANOUT dma-buf as a renderable image sibling. Verified present on the failing hosts, so these are not the cause: - `nvidia-drm.modeset = Y`; `/dev/dri/card0` + `renderD128` present - X server exposes DRI2 + DRI3 - `nvidia-drm_gbm.so` GBM backend (`libnvidia-allocator`) - EGL: `EGL_EXT_image_dma_buf_import`, `EGL_EXT_image_dma_buf_import_modifiers`, `EGL_MESA_image_dma_buf_export` - Vulkan: `VK_EXT_image_drm_format_modifier` (rev 2), `VK_EXT_external_memory_dma_buf`, `VK_EXT_queue_family_foreign`, `VK_KHR_external_memory_fd` - `app.getGPUFeatureStatus()` at paint time: `gpu_compositing=enabled vulkan=enabled_on webgl=enabled opengl=enabled_on rasterization=enabled_force` Ruled out: - All four `sharedTexturePixelFormat` values (`argb`, `nv12`, `rgba`, `bgra`) — identical result. - `--enable-native-gpu-memory-buffers` — no effect; it gates the client-side mmap path (`ui/gfx/linux/client_native_pixmap_dmabuf.cc`), while the viz capture pool uses `always_create_native_gmb_handle=true` and never consults it. - `--use-angle=gl` vs `--use-angle=vulkan` — no effect (both report the same ANGLE/Vulkan renderer on these hosts). - Initially-hidden window — `paintWhenInitiallyHidden: true` is set and `paint` does fire. The Linux `NativePixmapHandle` branch in `shell/browser/osr/osr_video_consumer.cc` looks correct, so this does not appear to be missing Electron code — the mismatch is upstream, between what the capture pool requests and what NVIDIA's GBM/Vulkan will import. Filing here because this is where it surfaces and because `docs/api/structures/shared-texture-handle.md` lists `nativePixmap` as Linux-supported without noting it does not work on the NVIDIA proprietary driver. Possibly related: #49247.

<!-- end-of-life -->

Hello @sdkv2. Thanks for reporting this and helping to make Electron better!

The version of Electron reported in this issue has reached end-of-life and is [no longer supported](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/electron-timelines#timeline). If you're still experiencing this issue on a [supported version](https://www.electronjs.org/releases/stable) of Electron, please update this issue to reflect that version of Electron.

Now adding the https://github.com/electron/electron/labels/blocked%2Fneed-info%20%E2%9D%8C label for this reason. This issue will be closed in 10 days if the above is not addressed.

Retested on **Electron 43.2.0** (currently supported) — the issue reproduces identically, so I've updated the version field above.

```
Electron 43.2.0 · Ubuntu 22.04.5 · kernel 6.8.0-59 · NVIDIA 575.51.03 · RTX 3060 · X11 (DRI3 present, nvidia-drm.modeset=Y)

details.texture : null
ANGLE           : Internal Vulkan error (-8) in DmaBufImageSiblingVkLinux.cpp, initImpl:616
```

Same result with `--enable-features=Vulkan`, which additionally leaves the page with no WebGL2 context.

The only difference from the 40.10.6 run is the ANGLE line number (614 → 616); it's the same function and the same `VK_ERROR_FEATURE_NOT_PRESENT`.

nodes.title: [Bug]: Main process crashes when onBeforeRequest redirects a CORS preflight

nodes.body:
Confirmed that this issue also reproduces on macOS with `SIGSEGV`.

The crash occurs because `ContinueToStartRequest` invokes `HandleBeforeRequestRedirect()` for preflight requests when `current_request_uses_header_client_` is true, leading to a NULL pointer dereference on `target_client_`.

Submitted PR #52611, which adds the missing `for_cors_preflight_` guard in `ContinueToStartRequest` to safely terminate preflight redirects with `net::ERR_FAILED`.

@talshalti Is the provided code in the description enough to reproduce the issue for you? If so, would it be possible for you to make a standalone testcase using [Electron Fiddle](https://www.electronjs.org/fiddle)? A working Electron Fiddle [gist](https://gist.github.com) would help greatly to confirm that we are both testing in the same way. Additionally, can you provide your full stack trace for the crash and not just excerpts?

I'm adding the `blocked/need-info` label for this reason. After you make a test case, please link to it in a follow-up comment.

@mlaurencin 
https://gist.github.com/talshalti/f5bdc323886393ee26bee70b53069986

the bug reproduces with the minimal code provided

Theres a reproducing gist added you can safely test it in case you want to

@talshalti I was responding to the question of how to override the decision to close the PR. It appears the author might have issues validating the fix locally before making the PR. If you would like to open a new PR with the same changes, the way to ensure it will not be closed is by doing as I stated.

I opened a PR:
https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/53127
can any of the commentators review it?
Fixed by #53294 and backported to 43-x-y, 44-x-y, and 45-x-y. #53127 contained the earlier focused fix and regression test. This issue can now be closed.

nodes.title: [Bug]: macOS 26.4 (Tahoe): browser process never exits after quit if a BrowserWindow was ever created — infinite usleep poll loop after all teardown completes
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the Contributing Guidelines for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the Code of Conduct that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.2.0 (also reproduced on 42.8.0, 43.1.0, and 44.0.0-alpha.8 — see below)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26.4.1 (Tahoe)

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

None on macOS 26.4.1 — every version tested (42.8.0, 43.1.0, 43.2.0, 44.0.0-alpha.8) hangs 5/5. The same versions exit cleanly on earlier macOS, so the regression is OS-version-gated, not Electron-version-gated.

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

Unknown — not systematically tested. The stall is in Electron Framework code (unsymbolicated Chromium teardown frames), so Chrome may carry a different shutdown path or a fix.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/bofeizhu/f91f42f580632ecff84b393ef939e66a (both mains, the EXIT/HANG runner, and the full `sample` output of a hanging 44.0.0-alpha.8 process)

### Expected Behavior

After `app.quit()` completes, the process exits.

### Actual Behavior

If the app **ever created a BrowserWindow** (even a single hidden one that only loaded `about:blank`), the main process never exits after quitting. The window closes, the Dock entry disappears, every JS lifecycle stage completes normally in milliseconds — `before-quit`, window close, `will-quit`, `quit`, and even Node's `process.on('exit')` — and the process then idles forever holding 100–150 MB RSS, spinning in a native usleep poll loop, at ~0% CPU.

With **no window at all**, the identical quit path exits cleanly with code 0 in ~1 s, 5/5.

Key observations:

- **Unbounded**: the process is still alive after 6.5 minutes; there is no timeout guard. Only SIGKILL ends it.
- **It is not waiting on children**: during the hang, the renderer helper exits first, then the GPU process and NetworkService utility helpers exit on their own within the first minute. After that the browser process is completely alone — no children, no windows — and still never exits.
- **Emergency exits hang identically**: calling `process.exit(0)` or `app.exit(0)` from the `quit` event produces the same stall, so the loop runs during native `exit()`/atexit/static-destructor teardown, past the last point where JS can run.
- **Stack signature**: `sample <pid>` during the hang shows 100% of samples (2612/2612 over 3 s) on the main thread in the identical stack — a chain of unsymbolicated Electron Framework frames with the leaf in `usleep` (libsystem_c). No modal/NSAlert, no dispatch-queue wait. Sample file attached.
- Reproduced 5/5 on each of Electron 42.8.0, 43.1.0, 43.2.0, and 44.0.0-alpha.8, in two independent investigation sessions on separate days.

Because the trigger is "a scene-backed NSWindow existed at some point," this looks like the macOS 26 scene-window teardown family (cf. #52437, which is a *different* signature: a runtime `performAsyncAndWait` dispatch deadlock while the app is unresponsive — here the app is responsive to the end, all teardown succeeds, and only the final process exit stalls). Also distinct from #49261 (macOS force-SIGKILLing running Electron apps). Presumably some teardown routine polls for a scene/WindowServer acknowledgment that macOS 26.4 no longer delivers.

### Steps to Reproduce

`main-hidden.js` — hangs 5/5:

```js
const { app, BrowserWindow } = require('electron');

app.whenReady().then(async () => {
  const win = new BrowserWindow({ show: false });
  await win.loadURL('about:blank');
  setTimeout(() => app.quit(), 500);
});

app.on('window-all-closed', () => app.quit());
app.on('quit', () => console.log('QUIT_EVENT_FIRED'));
```

`main-nowindow.js` — control, exits cleanly 5/5:

```js
const { app } = require('electron');

app.whenReady().then(() => {
  setTimeout(() => app.quit(), 500);
});

app.on('quit', () => console.log('QUIT_EVENT_FIRED'));
```

1. On macOS 26.4.x (arm64), `npm i electron@43.2.0` (or any version listed above).
2. `./node_modules/electron/dist/Electron.app/Contents/MacOS/Electron main-hidden.js`
3. Observe `QUIT_EVENT_FIRED` printed at ~900 ms; the command never returns. `ps` shows the process alive at ~0% CPU indefinitely; `sample` shows the usleep poll loop.
4. Run `main-nowindow.js` the same way: exits with code 0 in ~1 s.

A small runner that spawns Electron N times and reports EXIT/HANG with timings is included in the gist (`run.js`).

### Additional Information

- Real-world impact: any Electron app on macOS 26.4 leaves a zombie main process holding hundreds of MB every time the user quits. We currently work around it by SIGKILLing our own process from the `quit` event.
- Happy to re-run the harness against any branch/build that might help bisect.

Additional data: I ran the repro across GitHub Actions' macOS runner images (Electron 43.2.0, 3 runs per scenario per OS). Repro repo with the workflow: https://github.com/bofeizhu/electron-quit-hang-repro — run: https://github.com/bofeizhu/electron-quit-hang-repro/actions/runs/30708934473

| Environment | macOS | no-window | hidden about:blank window |
|---|---|---|---|
| GH runner (VM, arm64) | 14.8.7 | exits 0, 3/3 | **exits 0, 3/3** |
| GH runner (VM, arm64) | 15.7.7 | exits 0, 3/3 | **exits 0, 3/3** |
| GH runner (VM, arm64) | 26.5.2 | exits 0, 3/3 | **exits 0, 3/3** |
| Physical Mac (arm64) | 26.4.1 | exits 0, 5/5 | **hangs 5/5** |

Two takeaways:

1. The pre-Tahoe claim in the report is now measured, not inferred: identical binaries and scripts exit cleanly on 14.x and 15.x.
2. The **26.5.2 runner does not reproduce the hang**. Either the stall was fixed in a macOS 26.5.x update, or it does not manifest in virtualized runner environments (paravirtual GPU / different WindowServer interaction) — the 26.x data points differ in both OS version and physical-vs-VM, so they don't separate those variables. If anyone on physical hardware running 26.4.x or 26.5.x can run the gist repro (https://gist.github.com/bofeizhu/f91f42f580632ecff84b393ef939e66a), that would pin down whether this is version-bounded. I'll report back once this machine can be updated to 26.5.

Follow-up as promised: the physical Mac that reproduced this 5/5 has been updated from 26.4.1 to **macOS 26.6 (25G72)**, and the hang is **gone** — same Electron binaries (43.2.0 and 44.0.0-alpha.8), same repro scripts, hidden-window case now exits 0 in ~1s, 5/5 on both versions.

Combined with the earlier matrix (26.5.2 VM runner clean), this looks like an OS-side defect bounded to macOS 26.4.x, fixed by Apple in a later 26.5.x/26.6 update — not an Electron regression and not a VM artifact. Physical-hardware data on 26.5.x specifically is still missing, but from this machine's perspective the issue is resolved by updating macOS.

Happy for maintainers to close this, or keep it open as a known-issue reference for users pinned on 26.4.x.

The Windows overwrite confirmation appears and is dismissed automatically without user input. The existing target file is not locked by another process.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fd00a3aa-e650-4e3d-8b7e-8f39b6d4cbb5

A standalone testcase is provided as a ZIP attachment.

**Testcase ZIP:** [electron-save-dialog-repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30568973/electron-save-dialog-repro.zip)

1. Extract the ZIP file.
2. Run `pnpm install`, then `pnpm start`.
3. Click **Show save dialog**.
4. Keep the default filename, click **Save**, and observe the overwrite confirmation.

Minimal source:

`package.json`:

```json
{
  "name": "electron-save-dialog-sharing-violation-repro",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "private": true,
  "main": "main.js",
  "scripts": {
    "start": "electron ."
  },
  "devDependencies": {

  }
}
```

`main.js`:

```js
const { app, dialog } = require("electron");
const fs = require("node:fs");
const path = require("node:path");

app.whenReady().then(async () => {
  const target = path.join(app.getPath("downloads"), "electron-save-dialog-repro.zip");
  fs.writeFileSync(target, "overwrite confirmation reproduction\r\n");
  const result = await dialog.showSaveDialog({
    defaultPath: target,
    filters: [{ name: "ZIP archive", extensions: ["zip"] }]
  });

  fs.rmSync(target, { force: true });
  app.quit();
});
```

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/common-file-dialog#onshareviolation-and-onoverwrite

Electron's Windows implementation creates `IFileSaveDialog` with `FOS_OVERWRITEPROMPT`:

https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/shell/browser/ui/file_dialog_win.cc

nodes.title: [Bug]: Right-clicking a drag region in a window with no native title bar crashes the main process on macOS
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the Contributing Guidelines for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the Code of Conduct that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 42.0.1 ### What operating system(s) are you using? macOS ### Operating System Version macOS 26.5.2 (25F84), arm64 (M5) ### What arch are you using? arm64 ### Last Known Working Electron version Unknown — I've only tested 42.0.1. ### Expected Behavior Right-clicking a `-webkit-app-region: drag` region in a window with `titleBarStyle: 'hidden'` should do nothing (or show a window menu), and certainly shouldn't terminate the app. ### Actual Behavior The main process segfaults immediately and the app dies. It's a null dereference in Chromium's views layer, reached straight from AppKit event dispatch: ``` Exception Type: EXC_BAD_ACCESS (SIGSEGV) Exception Subtype: KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS at 0x0000000000000000 Triggered by Thread: 0 CrBrowserMain, Dispatch Queue: com.apple.main-thread ``` Symbolicated against `electron-v42.0.1-darwin-arm64-symbols.zip` (the module UUID in the report matches the shipped framework), innermost frame first: ``` views::internal::RootView::UpdateCursor(ui::MouseEvent const&) <- crash views::internal::RootView::OnMouseReleased(ui::MouseEvent const&) views::Widget::OnMouseEvent(ui::MouseEvent*) -[BridgedContentView mouseEvent:] -[NativeWidgetMacNSWindow sendEvent:] -[ElectronNSWindow sendEvent:] -[NSApplication(NSEventRouting) sendEvent:] -[AtomApplication sendEvent:] -[NSApplication _handleEvent:] -[NSApplication run] ``` Registers at the fault: `far: 0x0`, `x8: 0x0`, `esr: 0x92000006 (Data Abort) byte read Translation fault`. `RootView::UpdateCursor` looks up a view for the event location and asks it for a cursor, so a null result from that lookup for a point in the drag region would produce exactly this. I haven't verified that specific line, though — that's inference from the stack rather than something I've confirmed. ### Testcase Gist URL Not a gist, but the whole reproduction is below. `package.json`: ```json { "name": "titlebar-rightclick-repro", "version": "1.0.0", "main": "main.js" } ``` `main.js`: ```js const { app, BrowserWindow } = require('electron') app.whenReady().then(() => { const win = new BrowserWindow({ width: 800, height: 500, titleBarStyle: 'hidden', trafficLightPosition: { x: 12, y: 16 }, }) win.loadURL( 'data:text/html,' + encodeURIComponent(`
right-click anywhere in this strip

right-clicking below the strip is fine

`) ) }) ``` Run it, then right-click the dark strip. The app dies instantly, every time. ### Additional Information Right-clicking anywhere in the drag region crashes it, **including directly on the traffic-light buttons**. Right-clicking outside the drag region (the page content below) does not. I tried a few variations to narrow down what's needed. Both ingredients seem to be required — a drag region, in a window with no native title bar: | Window config | `-webkit-app-region: drag` present | Right-click in that region | | --- | --- | --- | | `titleBarStyle: 'hidden'` | yes | **crash** | | default (framed) | yes | no crash | | `titleBarStyle: 'hidden'` | no | no crash | | `frame: false` | yes | **crash** | With the default framed window I also right-clicked the real macOS title bar, which was fine. Worth noting that `frame: false` is affected too, not just `titleBarStyle: 'hidden'` — the crash from that variant is identical to the `'hidden'` one across the entire stack, not just the inner frames. That probably widens the impact quite a bit, since custom chrome via `frame: false` is common. I found this because GitHub Desktop 3.6.3 — which uses a hidden title bar with a drag region — crashes whenever its title bar is right-clicked. I have seven crash reports from that app, all byte-identical to each other (same 25 frames, same image offsets), and the crash from the minimal repro above matches them exactly across the Electron/Chromium frames, with only the outer application frames differing as you'd expect. So the signature looks deterministic rather than a race. Since a bare Electron app reproduces it, this doesn't look app-specific, and presumably affects any Electron app using a drag-region title bar on this macOS version.
This appears to be a duplicate of #51576, which was resolved with #51586. Please consider updating your Electron version.

Thanks for the pointer — you're right, this is a duplicate of #51576, fixed by #51586 and backported to `42-x-y` in #51605. My search didn't turn that up before filing; apologies for the noise.

For anyone who lands here from a search, I confirmed the fix covers this case:

- The fix shipped in **42.1.0** ("Fixed a crash on MacOS when a user clicked into a title bar or top view").
- I was on **42.0.1**, released a week earlier, which is why it still reproduced.
- Re-running the exact repro from this issue on 42.1.0 — both `titleBarStyle: 'hidden'` and `frame: false`, each with a `-webkit-app-region: drag` region — no longer crashes.

I ran into it via GitHub Desktop 3.6.3, which pins 42.0.1; I've pointed them at this in desktop/desktop#22624.

Closing as a duplicate.

nodes.title: docs: clarify D3D11 synchronization contract for Windows OffscreenSharedTexture
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the contribution documentation for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the code of conduct that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker for an issue that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.2.0

### Operating System

Windows 11 x64

### Description

The Windows `OffscreenSharedTexture` documentation describes `sharedTextureHandle` as a handle to a shared D3D11 texture and requires consumers to call `texture.release()` when finished. However, it does not describe the producer-to-consumer GPU synchronization guarantee at the time the `paint` event is emitted.

For ARGB/ABGR, Electron creates the resource with `D3D11_RESOURCE_MISC_SHARED_NTHANDLE` and deliberately does not use `D3D11_RESOURCE_MISC_SHARED_KEYEDMUTEX`:

https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v43.2.0/patches/chromium/osr_shared_texture_remove_keyed_mutex_on_win_dxgi.patch

An external native consumer currently follows this sequence:

```cpp
// The HANDLE is received from the paint event.
ComPtr<ID3D11Texture2D> texture;
device1->OpenSharedResource1(
    sharedTextureHandle,
    IID_PPV_ARGS(&texture));

// Read the texture on an external D3D11 device, for example:
context->CopyResource(destination.Get(), texture.Get());

// After the external operation is complete:
// texture.release() in Electron.
```

The JavaScript texture payload exposes no keyed-mutex key, fence, or sync token. The Chromium patch notes that Chromium will not write to the shared texture after its copy request returns, but it is not clear what guarantees that this GPU work is complete and visible to another D3D11 device when the JavaScript `paint` event is delivered.

### Questions

1. When the `paint` event is emitted, is the Windows ARGB/ABGR shared texture guaranteed to be immediately readable by another D3D11 device after `OpenSharedResource1`?
2. What synchronization or ordering primitive provides producer-to-consumer visibility in the mutex-free path?
3. If the external consumer must wait or synchronize before reading, what is the supported procedure?
4. Is keeping the texture object alive until the external GPU operation completes, followed by `texture.release()`, sufficient?

It would be helpful to document this contract in `offscreen-shared-texture.md`, because without it external D3D11 consumers cannot distinguish a supported read sequence from one that only happens to work on a particular driver.

### Expected Behavior

The documentation states the supported synchronization sequence and the point at which an external D3D11 consumer may safely read the shared texture.

### Actual Behavior

The handle type and release requirement are documented, but GPU read-readiness and cross-device synchronization are unspecified.

### Testcase Gist URL

N/A - this is a request to clarify the synchronization contract for the existing API.

<!-- end-of-life -->

Hello @guoxianzhe. Thanks for reporting this and helping to make Electron better!

The version of Electron reported in this issue has reached end-of-life and is [no longer supported](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/electron-timelines#timeline). If you're still experiencing this issue on a [supported version](https://www.electronjs.org/releases/stable) of Electron, please update this issue to reflect that version of Electron.

Now adding the https://github.com/electron/electron/labels/blocked%2Fneed-info%20%E2%9D%8C label for this reason. This issue will be closed in 10 days if the above is not addressed.

Updated the report to Electron 43.2.0, the current stable release. I also verified the current `v43.2.0` source: the Windows OSR ARGB/ABGR path is still mutex-free in `osr_shared_texture_remove_keyed_mutex_on_win_dxgi.patch`, while `offscreen-shared-texture.md` still documents the handle and release requirement but not the cross-device GPU synchronization/read-readiness contract. Therefore the documentation question applies to a currently supported Electron version.
